clue.text: Disney film buff beginning to tour continent

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or fan

indicators.note: beginning to tour asks for the opening letter of that word

parts.note: Asia is a continent

explanation.surface: A film fan sets off on a tour of a whole continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to tour' gives T, the first letter of 'tour'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is the 1940 Disney animated feature set to classical music.

clue.text: Consequences of dithering at the farm

indicators.note: dithering suggests wavering back and forth, so the letters of at the farm are jumbled

explanation.surface: Indecision on the farm has had its consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dithering' rearranges the nine letters of AT THE FARM.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftermath is the set of results that follow an event, its consequences.

clue.text: Carrying capacity of horse in normal muscle condition

indicators.note: in places the horse inside the word for normal muscle condition

parts.note: muscle tone is the normal slight tension of a resting muscle
a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.surface: A vet assesses a horse's load capacity by checking its muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'normal muscle condition' is one phrase: muscle tone is the healthy resting tension. 'in' is the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage measures how much cargo a ship can carry, its capacity in tons.

clue.text: Fur is a blessing to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that wearing fur is, in a way, a blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some extent' points to the letters running across 'iS A BLEssing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the prized dark pelt of a small Siberian marten.

clue.text: For listeners, everything a boring person needs

indicators.note: for listeners says the word for everything is only heard, so its sound gives the spelling entered

parts.note: everything means all

explanation.surface: Seemingly, a dull person needs everything you tell them.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'boring person' is not a dull one but someone who bores holes; an awl is the tool they need.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool used for piercing holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Fish served to wit, among other dishes

indicators.note: among puts the abbreviation for to wit inside the word for dishes

parts.note: pies are dishes of a different kind from the fish
sc., short for Latin scilicet, means to wit or namely

explanation.surface: At dinner, fish is served, along with other dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wit' is the Latin scilicet, abbreviated sc. and meaning namely; 'among' is the container indicator and 'served' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisces, the zodiac sign, is Latin for the Fishes and is represented by two fish.

clue.text: Participant in game show given some glass still drunk

parts.note: a pane is a single sheet of window glass

indicators.note: drunk suggests unsteady, so the letters of still are scrambled

explanation.surface: A game-show contestant is handed a glass while still tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like it describes a contestant but is the anagram indicator; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A panellist is one of the team members on a TV or radio quiz panel.

clue.text: Cricket side's drive initially bringing unplanned benefit

indicators.note: initially says the word for drive comes first, before the cricket side

parts.note: a spin is a short drive in a car, as in going for a spin
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team's attacking stroke at the start brings an unexpected bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' tempts as a batting stroke, and 'off drive' is one; here it is a jaunt in a car. The OFF side in cricket is the half of the field facing the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin-off is a by-product or incidental advantage arising from something else.

clue.text: English Liberal abandoning frivolous crew

indicators.note: abandoning says the Liberal letter leaves the word for frivolous

parts.note: light means frivolous or trivial

explanation.surface: An English Liberal politician quits a lighthearted team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' signals the Liberal leaving; 'crew' means a rowing eight, not a ship's company.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing eight is a boat with eight oarsmen, so the term names the whole crew.

clue.text: Stagger, taking bananas back

indicators.note: back says the word for bananas is written backwards

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, or nuts

explanation.surface: Someone staggers off carrying a load of bananas back.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish or amaze them, to stun.

clue.text: Itch to introduce initiator of sound effects

indicators.note: to introduce says the itch phrase leads in, put before the next letter

parts.note: to itch for something is to be longing for it

indicators.note: the initiator of sound is the letter that starts that word

explanation.surface: A craving to bring in someone to start the sound effects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Itch' is a verb here, giving BE LONGING; S comes from the start of 'sound'.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal effects are one's possessions, the things one owns.

clue.text: Fancy title given to book in exam

indicators.note: in puts title and book inside the word for exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a title is a name
NT, the New Testament, is a book in crossword usage

explanation.surface: A grand title is awarded to a book in an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: NAME and NT go 'in' ORAL; 'given to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as an adjective means decorative or elaborate, chiefly for show.

clue.text: Gale not shaking fruit

indicators.note: shaking signals that the letters of gale and not are tossed about

explanation.surface: The gale was not strong enough to shake the fruit off the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' rearranges GALE NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus fruit, a hybrid of tangerine and pomelo.

clue.text: It's a four-letter word, I swear it!

definitions.text: It's a four-letter word, I swear it!

parts.words: It's a four-letter word, I swear it!
parts.note: a four-letter word is usually a curse word, but this one is the four-letter word for a solemn sworn promise

explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn sworn declaration, and also a profane exclamation.

clue.text: Miller's rep coming to a dramatic conclusion?

definitions.text: Miller's rep coming to a dramatic conclusion?

parts.words: Miller's rep coming to a dramatic conclusion?
parts.note: Arthur Miller's play Death of a ... ends with its sales rep hero dying

explanation.walkthrough: 'Miller' suggests Chaucer's Miller or a flour miller, but it is the playwright Arthur Miller, whose Willy Loman dies at the end of the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A rep is a sales representative, a travelling seller of goods.

clue.text: Expedient, to get to work on time!

definitions.meaning: an expedient is a temporary stopgap measure

definitions.text: to get to work on time
definitions.meaning: to make a shift is to arrive for one's period of duty

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as MAKE SHIFT: to make it to your shift on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift is a crude temporary substitute adopted in an emergency.

clue.text: Popular with relatives at Caen he's escaped public disgrace

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: escaped says the French he gets out of the word for relatives

parts.note: relatives make up a family
il is French for he, Caen being a French city

explanation.surface: A man popular with his relatives in Normandy flees in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at Caen' says the word for 'he' is French; 'escaped' removes it. Caen is a city in Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is notoriety or public shame earned by wicked behaviour.

clue.text: Girl loses head over politician, allowing no option

indicators.note: over places the first piece above the second in this down clue
loses head says the girl's name drops its first letter

parts.note: Amanda is a girl's name
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A girl falls head over heels for a politician and has no choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' drops the first letter; 'over' works only because this is a down clue, so one piece sits above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandatory means compulsory, required with no choice permitted.

clue.text: Piercing cry makes butcher bird turn tail

indicators.note: turn tail says only the tail end of the bird's name is turned round

parts.note: the shrike is called the butcher bird because it impales prey on thorns

explanation.surface: A piercing cry makes a predatory bird flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn tail' reverses just the last two letters of SHRIKE, KE becoming EK.
explanation.definitionFit: A shriek is a shrill, high-pitched scream.

clue.text: Respiratory aid fitter puts up at home

indicators.note: puts up says the fitter word places the home word above itself in the down light

parts.note: in means at home
haler means healthier, more fit

explanation.surface: A plumber installs a breathing device in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'fitter' is not a tradesman here but the comparative adjective, HALER.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler is a device used to breathe in medication, as for asthma.

clue.text: Install Queen Elizabeth I as protector of north?

indicators.note: as protector of says the queen's letters surround and guard the abbreviation for north

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's cipher
NTH is an abbreviation for north
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Crowning Elizabeth I as a defender of the north.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the royal monogram of Elizabeth Regina; the abbreviation for north is the rare three-letter one. 'as protector of' is the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthrone is to place a monarch on the throne, installing them formally.

clue.text: Figure from refuge mostly boarding right vehicle

indicators.note: boarding says the shortened refuge gets on, going inside the other letters

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: mostly says the word for refuge loses its last letter

parts.note: a home is a refuge or shelter

explanation.surface: Someone from a shelter boards the correct bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts HOME to HOM, which goes 'boarding' R + BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a geometric figure with four equal sides.

clue.text: Monarch's quiet expression of a pleasure

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
ah is an exclamation of pleasure or satisfaction

explanation.surface: A king quietly sighs with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: The shah was the title of the hereditary ruler of Iran.

clue.text: Important takeover reported in this form of verse

indicators.note: reported says the phrase is spoken, and its sound gives the spelling

parts.note: high means important and a coup is a takeover of power

explanation.surface: News of a big takeover is relayed in poetic form.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH COUP said out loud sounds like HAIKU.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese poem of three lines with seventeen syllables.

clue.text: Eg Queen Mary's tax originally settled by western state

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free

indicators.note: originally asks for the first letter of settled

parts.note: Oman is a state in Arabia

explanation.surface: Queen Mary's taxes were first settled by a western state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Mary' suggests the ship, but it is Mary, Queen of Scots. SCOT survives in 'scot-free', without paying the tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary, Queen of Scots was a Scottish monarch, so she is an example of a woman from Scotland.

clue.text: Rope-maker extremely sceptical about savings plan

indicators.note: about says the end letters go round the savings plan
extremely asks for the first and last letters of sceptical

parts.note: an ISA, Individual Savings Account, is a British tax-free savings plan

explanation.surface: A doubtful ropemaker is wary of a savings plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives SL, which goes 'about' ISA. An ISA is a UK tax-free savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a fibre from an agave plant used for making rope and twine.

clue.text: American country house broken into by old criminal

indicators.note: broken says the house and American pieces are split open to take the other letters

parts.note: a villa is a large country house
US means American
into gives in

explanation.surface: An American's country house has been burgled by a former crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' opens VILLA + US to take IN (from 'into') and O; 'by' is a link. 'criminal' looks like a noun but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Villainous means wicked or criminal in nature.

clue.text: Sphere in which sibling is given a rise

indicators.note: given a rise says the word for sibling goes up the down light, reversing it

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a sibling

explanation.surface: A setting where a brother gets a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' is a link; 'given a rise' turns BRO upward in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a sphere or globe.

clue.text: Number three in aquarium feeding young male dolphin

indicators.note: feeding says the picked letter goes into the word for young male

parts.note: a boy is a young male

indicators.note: number three in asks for the third letter of aquarium

explanation.surface: A boy feeds a dolphin at the aquarium.
explanation.walkthrough: U, the third letter of 'aquarium', goes into BOY. 'dolphin' is not the animal but a mooring buoy or post.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is also a mooring post or buoy for securing boats.

clue.text: Part of tank track making comeback? About time

indicators.note: making comeback says the word for track runs backwards

parts.note: a rut is a track worn by wheels
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Part of a tank's tracks is coming back into service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' is the reversal indicator; 'Part of tank' refers to the military vehicle, not a water tank.
explanation.definitionFit: The turret is the rotating armoured top of a tank that houses the gun.

clue.text: A sucker for gold

definitions.meaning: a large hard peppermint sweet that one sucks
in archery the central gold ring of the target is called the gold

explanation.walkthrough: A 'sucker' is a sweet to suck, a British boiled mint humbug. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullseye is the centre of a target, which archers call the gold.
